description: First-person DOOM-style game where movement, turning, and collision are computed by stored circuits in titan.gguf. The browser is a pure container (paints + reads keys). The host injects the electron (input bits) and surfaces the output (result bits).

doom_move16.purpose: Movement, turning, and wall collision per tick
doom_move16.inputs: px(16) + py(16) + dx(16) + dy(16) + wall_x(1) + wall_y(1) + angle(8) + turn_left(1) + turn_right(1)

doom_map16.purpose: Level geometry lookup -- cell index to wall/empty

doom_raycast.purpose: Per-column raycast -- full visible-surface computation as one gate net
doom_raycast.note: The render circuit -- stored but not used by the live demo (DDA in the browser is the display crutch for real-time play). The circuit IS the computation; the browser raycast is presentation only.

host_boundary.inject_electron: Feed keypress-derived input bits into doom_move16 circuit
host_boundary.surface_output: Read new_px, new_py, new_angle from circuit output bits
host_boundary.display_crutch: Browser-side DDA raycaster for real-time visual presentation (labeled)

verification.method: Byte-exact comparison of circuit output vs Python reference implementation

launch.controls: W/S or Up/Down arrows to move, A/D or Left/Right arrows to turn

lineage: Based on build_05 (sdc_doom_server.py) -- the spec-compliant DOOM build where the server ripples the stored circuit and the browser is a pure container.
